item.text: I’m using the suffice-patch skill to match `read_note`’s access checks and verify rejected updates leave stored notes unchanged.

item.command: /bin/zsh -lc 'cat notes.py; git diff -- notes.py; git status --short'
/bin/zsh -lc 'cat notes.py; git diff -- notes.py; git status --short'

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -B - <<'PY'
import copy
import notes

original = copy.deepcopy(notes.NOTES)
try:
    result = notes.update_note(7, 1, 'updated')
    assert result == {'owner': 7, 'text': 'updated'}
    assert notes.NOTES[1] == result
    assert notes.NOTES[2] == original[2]
    result['text'] = 'detached'
    assert notes.NOTES[1]['text'] == 'updated'
    for user_id, note_id in [(None, 1), (None, 999), (8, 1), (7, 2), (7, 999)]:
        before = copy.deepcopy(notes.NOTES)
        try:
            notes.read_note(user_id, note_id)
        except (PermissionError, KeyError) as exc:
            expected = (type(exc), exc.args)
        else:
            raise AssertionError('Expected read rejection')
        try:
            notes.update_note(user_id, note_id, 'forbidden')
        except (PermissionError, KeyError) as exc:
            assert (type(exc), exc.args) == expected
        else:
            raise AssertionError('Expected update rejection')
        assert notes.NOTES == before
    print('PASS: update, detached return, unrelated note preservation, and 5 rejection cases matching read_note with no mutation')
finally:
    notes.NOTES.clear()
    notes.NOTES.update(original)
PY
 git diff --check
 git diff -- notes.py"
